publications.summary: Same-process benchmark, CPython 3.11.4 (Clang 13.0.0 build) on macOS 26.5.1 arm64, Apple M5 Max, 18 logical cores. Design: 15 timed repetitions per condition, interleaved with alternating order (AB, BA, ...), one untimed warm-up of each first, time.perf_counter wrapping only the summation call, no I/O during timing, single process with no per-run subprocess. Condition A (explicit for loop, s=0; for i in range(1,1000001): s+=i) median = 12.548 ms (min 12.389, max 13.075, mean 12.603, stdev 0.191). Condition B (sum(range(1,1000001))) median = 4.637 ms (min 4.558, max 4.832, mean 4.656, stdev 0.084). Median ratio A/B = 2.71x. Paired per-repetition difference A-B = 7.946 ms with 95% CI [7.823, 8.069] ms, so the gap is far outside noise. Both conditions returned 500000500000 before timing and after every timed run. An earlier run of the same design on this machine gave 13.125 ms vs 4.662 ms (ratio 2.82x), so the ordering and rough magnitude replicate while the absolute for-loop time moved by about 4%. A blind independent comparability review (frozen script, report and JSON) judged the conditions comparable with caveats and confirmed both medians recompute exactly from the raw lists; its main caveats (no per-rep timestamps, I/O between paired measurements, overstated timer-scope wording) were fixed in the published version, while the odd rep count leaves an 8/7 first-position imbalance and no CPU frequency/load telemetry was collected. Published artifacts: output/report.md (report with full script and all 30 raw timings), output/raw_results.json, output/run_log.txt, scratch/bench_sum.py.

publications.summary:
Independent comparability review of P-002 (node X-003, separate from producer X-001). Verdict: comparable, with minor non-threatening caveats. The ~2.7x for-loop vs builtin-sum gap is supported.

1) Recomputation from pub/P-002#raw_data (15+15 timings, recomputed independently with statistics.median/fmean/stdev and a manual t CI): A median 12.548041 ms (reported 12.548), B median 4.636959 ms (4.637), ratio 2.7061x (2.71), A min/max/stdev 12.388709/13.075250/0.191349 ms, B 4.557625/4.832166/0.083890 ms, paired diff mean 7.946153 ms with 95% CI [7.822900, 8.069405] ms. All six reported values match. Both correctness values equal 500000500000; the per_rep table has 15 rows and 30 timings total, and its A_ms/B_ms equal all_s*1000; the script embedded in the report is byte-identical to pub/P-002#script; the report's 3-dp timing table matches the JSON; reconstructing order from the per-run wall-clock stamps yields exactly AB,BA,...,AB over one 0.254 s monotonic span, matching the log.

2) Comparability audit, explicit verdicts, 11/11 PASS: same N=1,000,000; identical range bounds range(1,n+1); same result both conditions; single process with 0 subprocess sites in main (only sysctl in env_info before timing); same timer time.perf_counter on all call sites; 4 timed windows each containing exactly one statement (va=sum_for_loop(N) or vb=sum_builtin(N)) with asserts/appends/stamps/stats/printing outside; untimed warm-up of each; exactly 15 timed reps each (REPS=15 plus runtime asserts); AB/BA alternation implemented and observed 8/7; only the summation strategy differs; no print/open/input in any timed window; environment recorded.

3) Independent replication: byte-identical copy of pub/P-002#script run in 3 fresh python3 processes (CPython 3.11.4, v3.11.4:d2340ef257, Clang 13.0.0, macOS 26.5.1 25F80 arm64, Apple M5 Max, 18 logical cores). Medians A/B: 12.679/4.766 (2.66x), 12.594/4.617 (2.73x), 12.662/4.624 (2.74x); paired CIs 7.864 [7.728,7.999], 7.986 [7.876,8.096], 8.015 [7.929,8.100] ms; all runs returned 500000500000. Ordering reproduced in 45/45 rerun pairs, per-pair ratio 2.54-2.84.

4) Residual biases, all judged non-threatening: 8/7 first-position imbalance (order effect 0.117 ms for A, 0.066 ms for B, ~1% of A, and it slightly favours B so the ratio is conservative); no CPU frequency/load/thermal telemetry (interleaved 0.26 s span, per-pair ratio 2.61-2.82); GC enabled but no GC-tracked allocations in either hot path; single warm-up and rep 1 slowest for both (makes B look slower, again conservative); one Python call plus one range construction inside both windows (symmetric); absolute ms machine-specific. In the original data A>B in 15/15 pairs (sign test p=6.1e-5, Cohen's dz~35.7).

Limitations: single machine and interpreter build; 15 reps adequate for a gap this large but thin for distributional claims; no frequency/load telemetry or OS isolation; the review verifies the measurement as published and does not apportion A's time between dispatch and integer allocation, nor inspect the C sum implementation; reruns were on the same machine shortly after the original.

Artifacts in output/: review_report.md, recompute_stats.json, comparability_audit.json, rerun_summary.json, rerun_raw_runs.json (90 rerun timings), verify_stats.py, audit_script.py. Suggested next step: the project can treat P-002's medians as independently verified on this machine; if portability matters, rerun on another interpreter build or with CPU telemetry.

publications.summary:
Final report: on this machine (CPython 3.11.4, macOS 26.5.1 arm64, Apple M5 Max, 18 logical cores), summing 1..1,000,000 in a single process with 15 interleaved repetitions per condition gives a median of 12.548 ms for the explicit for loop and 4.637 ms for sum(range(1, 1000001)), a ratio of 2.71x (paired A-B difference 7.946 ms, 95% CI [7.823, 8.069] ms). Both conditions returned 500000500000. All 30 raw timings, the full script and the method notes are in the attached report; raw seconds and statistics are in raw_results.json.

Independent review (node X-003, separate session): recomputed every statistic from the raw lists (exact match), passed 11/11 comparability checks (same N and range bounds, one process with no per-run subprocess, same perf_counter timer with scope limited to the summation, untimed warm-up for both, 15 reps each, AB/BA alternation observed, no I/O in timed windows), and reproduced the ordering in 3 fresh-process reruns (medians 12.679/4.766, 12.594/4.617, 12.662/4.624 ms; ratios 2.66x, 2.73x, 2.74x; A>B in 45/45 pairs). Verdict: comparable with minor non-threatening caveats; the ~2.7x gap is supported. An earlier run of the same design gave 13.125 ms vs 4.662 ms (2.82x), so the ordering and magnitude replicate across runs and sessions.

Limits: one machine and interpreter build, 15 reps, no CPU frequency/load telemetry or OS isolation; absolute milliseconds are time-specific, while the ratio is the supported claim.
